Hanukkah, the Festival of Lights, is a Jewish celebration of resilience and tradition. Rooted in a miracle in which oil lit a lamp for 8 days even though it was only enough for one, it’s a time for family gatherings, lighting the menorah, and indulging in treats like sufganiyot and latkes.


Gift giving is a more recent addition to Hanukkah traditions.[Gelt](https://www.1800eichlers.com/blog/hanukkah-gelt/296639?srsltid=AU7gw4VGAJCJyRHc-F5OlrAa1f-Nvgr9ZfSjAs8cZ-fo-TLMcQKXwnl6) , small amounts of money given to Torah teachers and students, has been part of the holiday since the 1600s in Eastern Europe, but wrapped presents didn't become common until the mid-20th century. This is when American Jewish families started giving gifts alongside the older custom of gelt, largely in response to[the popularity of gift giving at Christmas](https://time.com/5747552/hanukkah-gifts-history/) .


In 2026,[Hanukkah begins](https://www.hebcal.com/holidays/chanukah-2026) at sundown on Friday, December 4 and ends at nightfall on Saturday, December 12. Hanukkah always starts on the 25th day of the Hebrew month of Kislev. Because the Jewish calendar is lunisolar, the dates shift annually, typically falling anywhere between late November and late December.


As a holiday that’s about much more than presents, Hanukkah is an opportunity for brands to engage with customers in a way that honors these traditions while also providing unique value.


Whether it’s highlighting exclusive products, offering a Hanukkah-themed gift guide, or creating campaigns centered around family, tradition, and the spirit of the season, there are plenty of ways to show your customers that your brand understands and respects the essence of Hanukkah.


Here are 8 Hanukkah marketing ideas, one for each candle on the menorah:


## 1. Show up in gift-related AI searches


Consumers are actively searching for the perfect gifts for their loved ones during the holidays. According to Klaviyo's 2026[State of the Holiday Buyer Report](https://www.klaviyo.com/bfcm/holiday-shopping-trends) , 67% of consumers say they already have a gift idea in mind before they start shopping.


When they do that, they’ll see a higher variety of product options on Google than they will with an LLM. But according to the same report, 1 in 4 shoppers are using AI to get personalized gift ideas or recommendations.


This means you’ll want your brand to show up in those[AI search](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/ai-search-trends) results, too. Here are a few ways to improve your brand's chances of showing up in[AI shopping](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/how-to-adapt-your-online-presence-for-ai-shopping) searches:


- **Write product descriptions like you're answering a question.** Rather than describing a product as a "wool blend scarf," try "a soft, wool blend scarf that keeps you warm on milder winter nights, in sizes to fit teens through adults." The more specific the use case, the more likely LLMs are to surface your product for a query like, "I need a cozy gift for grandma."
- **Add FAQs that answer real Hanukkah gifting questions.** Go beyond sizing and shipping. Answer questions like, "Is this a good gift for someone's first Hanukkah?" or, "Can this be personalized for a bar or bat mitzvah, too?" This gives LLMs full context to pull from for deeper queries.
- **Build gift guides organized by who people are shopping for.** A Hanukkah gift guide for coworkers under $30, for example, gives LLMs a direct match for how people actually search.
- **Ask for reviews that mention gifting.** Use[custom review questions](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/16319181846171) to prompt customers to leave more specific reviews, so LLMs can feature them in comparison guides and make life easier for shoppers when they’re considering multiple products.


### Hanukkah marketing example: ModernTribe structures their gift guide with specifics


[ModernTribe](https://moderntribe.com/) , a Judaica and Jewish gifts retailer, structures their Hanukkah gift guide in a way that's built to be found in AI search results. Rather than one Hanukkah gift category, the page categorizes products into smaller collections like Hanukkah decorations, Hanukkah candles for sale, and Hanukkah clothes: the same kind of natural language phrasing a shopper might type into ChatGPT or Gemini when asking for gift ideas.


[ModernTribe](https://moderntribe.com/pages/hanukkah-gifts)


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** The page also updates throughout the season and includes a real-time social proof pop-up showing recent purchases from other shoppers. Signals like these help both shoppers and LLMs contextualize the product recommendations.


## 2. Grow your subscriber lists with a Hanukkah contest or giveaway


Hanukkah's 8 nights give you a way to engage multiple segments of your audience on the channels they most want to engage with.


For example, you may have email subscribers who would rather interact with you via text message, but they don’t know they can. Or you may have Instagram followers who don’t know they could get exclusive perks and early access if they sign up for emails, text messages, or WhatsApp.


Consider launching an Instagram giveaway that asks your followers to[subscribe via DM](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/social) for a chance to enter. You can also ask them to tag a friend who doesn’t follow you yet, or tag you in a post of them using your product.


### Marketing example: Thirdlove offers a giveaway to grow their Instagram following


Intimates brand[Thirdlove](https://www.thirdlove.com/) ran an Instagram giveaway for a $300 gift certificate that required entrants to follow Thirdlove on social media, like the post, and tag a friend in a comment.


[Thirdlove Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/DcwHYKHDfMC/)


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** Consider giving away a product tied to Hanukkah to make your promotion seasonally appropriate. That could mean a limited-edition item in Hanukkah's traditional blue and white, a bundle of 8 items, or a food and drink gift box built for a Hanukkah gathering. Or, partner with an aligned brand to sweeten the deal and increase your reach.


Once you have people who are subscribed to multiple marketing channels, you can use AI-powered[channel affinity](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/what-is-channel-affinity) to determine which channels they’re most likely to engage with next.


## 3. Use vibe marketing to test Hanukkah promotions


[Vibe marketing](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/vibe-marketing-era) is AI prompt-based campaign creation that works with your data, brand guidelines, and other guardrails to create emails and text messages.


Ask your[AI marketing agent](https://www.klaviyo.com/composer) to help you bring your Hanukkah marketing campaigns to life with these example prompts:


- "Build a Hanukkah email that announces a one-night-only discount on the first night of the holiday, and segment it so VIP customers get early access."
- "Write 3 versions of a Hanukkah text message: one that uses humor, one that leans nostalgic and family-focused, and one that's straightforward and deal-driven, so I can test which tone performs best."
- "Build an omnichannel flow that sends a Hanukkah gift guide email 30 days before the holiday, follows up with a text message reminder a week later for anyone who hasn't opened it, and closes with a final text 5 days before Hanukkah for last-minute shoppers, timed to when and where each subscriber is most likely to engage."


### Hanukkah marketing example: GourmetGiftBaskets.com shares their holiday bundle


Artisanal gift basket brand[GourmetGiftBaskets.com](http://gourmetgiftbaskets.com/) , known for baskets packed with fresh fruit, fine wine, baked goods, and more, shares a themed gift basket in this Hanukkah marketing example.


This image works because it puts the gift basket directly into a Hanukkah scene, with a hand lighting a menorah at a table set with a wineglass and small plates. The background image adds context to signal that this is a gift for Hanukkah, better than a plain product shot on a white background would.


**Subject line:** Hanukkah Gifts That Arrive in Time


[Milled](https://milled.com/gourmetgiftbaskets.com/hanukkah-gifts-that-arrive-in-time-4J9qxMOTOAOmBO3R)


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** You don't need a full photoshoot for every product or every holiday to get a similar effect. An[AI photo editor](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/remix) can take one product photo and place it in different settings, like alongside a lit menorah, on a table set for a holiday dinner, or amid a pile of wrapped gifts.


With themed photos, you can test which scene resonates most, or reuse the same product photo across Hanukkah, Christmas, and other holidays without investing resources in a new shoot each time.


## 4. Use AI to quickly access Hanukkah audience segments


Sending the right messages to the right audience is a key part of any omnichannel marketing plan. People who bought a relevant item last year, clicked on a past Hanukkah campaign, or bought holiday items during late fall or early winter could be good candidates.


Your AI marketing agent can help you build more complex segments as part of creating your holiday campaign. Here are a couple examples:


- **Combine last year's Hanukkah purchases with this year's engagement.** Prompt your AI marketing agent to build a segment of customers who bought Judaica or gift items during last year's Hanukkah season, opened at least two campaign emails so far this year, and haven't purchased anything in the past 30 days.
- **Surface high-intent browsers early.** Ask your AI agent to identify customers who've viewed a Hanukkah collection page more than once in the past two weeks and added an item to their cart. This segment might need a last-minute nudge before the holiday starts.


### Hanukkah marketing example: Ministry of Supply targets last-minute shoppers


Apparel brand[Ministry of Supply](https://www.ministryofsupply.com/) targets last-minute shoppers in this Hanukkah marketing example. Their email leads with a headline built around timing: "Unsure of where to even begin... and they're already lighting the first candle?" The copy focuses on shoppers who haven't started buying gifts yet, even as the holiday is already underway.


Rather than one generic push, the email breaks up gift shopping into curated guides by persona, starting with "gifts for the pragmatist," so each recipient has a starting point when shopping.


**Subject line:** Happy Hanukkah. Hard to find a gift? We have a solution for that.


[Milled](https://milled.com/ministry-of-supply/happy-hanukkah-hard-to-find-a-gift-we-have-a-solution-for-that-G3n3ewzeDp1gQr2V)


## 5. Launch an AI customer agent that can recommend gifts for Hanukkah


The holidays are a busy time for customer service teams, and marketers often get some of the overflow questions in DMs. But when a shopper reaches out with a question like, "What should I buy my sister for Hanukkah?", that's an opportunity for autonomous service.


When it’s trained on your product catalog and brand guidelines, your[AI customer agent](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/customer-agent) can answer questions like that before anyone on your team even sees them. With access to your customer data, it can ask a personalized follow-up question or two, the same way a helpful store associate would, and land on a few options that actually fit.


If the shopper wants to keep narrowing down, say from "a Hanukkah gift for a coffee person" to a specific color mug, the AI agent can keep going within the conversation window.


### Hanukkah marketing example: Harney & Sons recommends Hanukkah teas through chat


Tea brand[Harney & Sons](https://www.harney.com/) has an AI customer agent on their website. In this Hanukkah marketing example, see how a shopper asks for a good tea to serve during Hanukkah. The AI agent names 3 options, then narrows choices down to a single top pick and offers to refine by preference (caffeine-free, giftable, or by tea type).


Every recommendation is grounded in Harney & Sons' actual product catalog. The shopper gets a shortlist of things to buy with direct calls to action rather than a search bar to figure it out on their own.


Harney & Sons


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** On top of personalized recommendations, your AI agent can answer common customer service questions about returns, loyalty points, promotions, and shipping details leading up to and after Hanukkah.


## 6. Share Hanukkah-inspired recipes


Food plays a special role in Hanukkah celebrations, making it a natural tie-in for Hanukkah marketing. Dishes like latkes and sufganiyot aren’t just delicious, they’re a nod to the miracle of Hanukkah.


Depending on what your brand sells and who you’re marketing to, you can share traditional recipes through emails or text messages using autonomous marketing. Ask your AI agent to tell you what segments would be the most inclined to respond to a recipe-related or Hanukkah-specific message and let it build out the messaging for you.


### Hanukkah marketing example: New West KnifeWorks shares a Hanukkah recipe


Premium knife brand[New West KnifeWorks](https://www.newwestknifeworks.com/?srsltid=AfmBOool2eya45sET15-atWWGYRYvWPk-s3TzOJGqwRLl7b3WdJ_zH5K) sent this Hanukkah email pairing a recipe with a seasonal offer.


**Subject line:** How To Make Our Favorite Chanukah Latkes!


[Milled](https://milled.com/newwestknifeworks.com/how-to-make-our-favorite-chanukah-latkes-Eol4SM496370_aCc)


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** This type of message is more impactful if the message is hyper-relevant to the recipient. Ask your AI marketing agent to create an email and text message campaign that swaps in different product recommendations or educational content based on what each customer has already purchased.


A first-time shopper who doesn't own an ironwood knife, for example, is a great fit for the 20% off call-out shown here. But a customer who already bought that set might respond better to a recommendation for a cutting board or an apron, since those are a more useful next purchase than a knife they already have.


## 7. Collect Hanukkah-themed reviews for future marketing campaigns


Reviews are the most influential factor for customers when making a first purchase, according to customers surveyed as part of Klaviyo’s 2025[Future of Consumer Marketing Report](https://www.klaviyo.com/marketing-resources/future-of-consumer-marketing) .


Of course, reviews need to be detailed and plentiful to influence purchase decisions. When customers land on your product pages, they want to see reviews that address their specific pain points at length and with photos.


For Hanukkah, get ahead of customer expectations by including holiday-themed reviews in your marketing messages. Depending on your industry, these reviews could include festive images of a holiday spread or detailed descriptions of the joy of receiving a gift.


### Hanukkah marketing example: Sloomoo Institute increases image-based UGC with an incentive


In this Hanukkah marketing example, see how[Sloomoo Institute](https://sloomooinstitute.com/) , an interactive, experiential space that calls itself “a celebration of sensory play,” embraces the Hanukkah spirit by creating themed slime kits. They developed slimes in traditional holiday colors, like blue and silver, and infused them with sparkles, charms, and even scents reminiscent of holiday treats.


They even add a little twist to their “Got Gelt” slime, inspired by the traditional Hanukkah gift gelt: a real or chocolate coin wrapped in gold foil. The email encourages those lucky enough to get the “Got Gelt” slime with real gelt inside to snap a photo, share it on their socials, and get another slime for free. This helps the team gather[user-generated content (UGC)](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/user-generated-content-ugc) and raise authentic brand awareness during the 8-day celebratory period.


[Milled](https://milled.com/sloomooinstitute-com/hanukkah-o-hannukah-qPu6PAQepkLfi_fL)


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** To collect these kinds of reviews for next year, build a[review request](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/review-management) flow timed to product usage. You may also want to offer an incentive for reviews that contain images, like[Compass Coffee](https://www.compasscoffee.com/) did when they boosted these review types[3.7x in one quarter](https://www.klaviyo.com/customers/case-studies/compass-coffee-reviews) .


## 8. Promote a Hanukkah-themed product


Promoting or creating a Hanukkah-themed product is a powerful way to connect with your audience during the season. By sharing something unique that resonates with the holiday’s traditions, you can meet market demand as well as earn trust with your audience.


[Segments](https://www.klaviyo.com/features/segmentation) of customers who buy from holiday-specific campaigns may be more likely to convert on similar campaigns in the future. When people click or buy products created for a specific purpose, you’re generating customer data that can produce more relevant offers down the line.


A Hanukkah-themed product doesn't have to be a menorah. Here are just a few other ideas:


- A flavor built around jelly donuts or chocolate gelt
- A candle scent that nods to the oil the holiday commemorates
- Packaging that leans into blue and silver instead of winter red and green


Figuring out which of those directions fits your brand is a good use for vibe marketing. Describe the mood you're going for and let your AI marketing agent draft a few concepts before you commit to one.


### Hanukkah marketing example: McConnell’s brings back its Genghis Cohen collab


A great Hanukkah marketing example is[McConnell's Fine Ice Creams](https://mcconnells.com/collections/fine-ice-creams) , an ice cream brand that's been scooping since 1949. For a second year, McConnell's teamed up with[Genghis Cohen](https://www.genghiscohen.com/) , a well-known Chinese restaurant in Los Angeles, for their holiday menu.


The pairing taps into a cultural tradition. Many Jewish Americans have eaten Chinese food on Christmas for well over a century, a habit that traces back to Jewish and Chinese immigrant communities living side by side on[New York's Lower East Side](https://www.history.com/articles/jews-chinese-food-christmas-immigrants-new-york) .


This release, Baby Got Mac(aroon), brings back toasted coconut macaroon cookies folded into coconut cream ice cream. The email leans fully into the holiday, with pints stacked next to a lit menorah and blue tinsel up top.


**Subject line:** Our Hanukkah Collab Is Back! 🕎


[Milled](https://milled.com/mcconnells.com/our-hanukkah-collab-is-back-A4OOOGMBl9Lr7AJI)

The top section, on a yellow-orange background, reads, "Now Scoopin' Baby Got Mac(aroon)," describing a Hanukkah collaboration with LA restaurant Genghis Cohen, now in its second year, with a "Shop Tradition" button. Below, a photo shows 3 pints of Baby Got Mac(aroon) ice cream stacked on a table surrounded by blue tinsel, next to a lit menorah with a hand placing a candle. The email ends with an "Order Now" button in red and white.


**Hanukkah marketing tip:** Rather than announcing the drop to their full list, McConnell's could email frequent holiday purchasers first, giving past buyers a head start on a flavor with limited availability. A returning collaboration gives customers something to look forward to year after year.
